subject: computer-organization-and-architecture

chosen.title: Lecture 33 - Input-Output Primitives
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (IIT Guwahati)
chosen.why: the only readable lecture that sets up the whole topic - why an interface exists, what a device controller is, and the three modes named before any of them is taught

chosen.title: Lecture 34 - Interrupt Driven I/O
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (IIT Guwahati)
covers: why programmed I/O wastes the CPU
chosen.why: states the programmed-I/O defect and the interrupt remedy in the same lecture, which is the comparison the cards are built on

chosen.title: Lecture 35 - DMA Transfer
chosen.channel: NPTEL, Computer Organization and Architecture - A Pedagogical Aspect (IIT Guwahati)
covers: removal of the processor from the data path
chosen.why: the clearest statement found of why DMA exists: the CPU cannot carry 1 KB through 8-16 registers, so the transfer must bypass it

chosen.title: I/O Organization & Interrupts (romanised Hindi)
chosen.why: the only source read this run that states the whole interrupt vocabulary - maskable, non-maskable, vectored, non-vectored, vector table - in one place, and it lists the misconceptions GATE exploits

chosen.title: System Buses & DMA (romanised Hindi)
covers: cycle stealing, burst and transparent modes
chosen.why: the only readable source that names all three DMA modes and states each one's cost to the CPU, and it corrects the common 'DMA interrupts per byte' error

chosen.title: Chapter 6 - Memory and Other I/O Topics (slide deck)
chosen.why: a university course deck read in part; it is the only source that covers the DMA/cache coherence and DMA/page-chunking consequences, which no GATE-oriented source mentions

chosen.title: I/O Interface (Interrupt and DMA Mode)
covers: DMA total time = request + transfer + release
chosen.why: read in full as a cross-check on the mode definitions; used for the DMA total-time expression and nothing else, since it is a secondary source

chosen.title: Computer Organization lecture notes (I/O and interrupt sections)
chosen.channel: Institute of Aeronautical Engineering, Computer Organization lecture notes
covers: why peripherals cannot join the system bus
chosen.why: gives the register-transfer form of the interrupt cycle and the HOLD/HLDA names, which the NPTEL transcripts only describe in words

rejected.why: NPTEL IIT Kharagpur Computer Organization lectures 24, 25 and 26 are exactly Programmed I/O, Interrupt Driven I/O and DMA, but only the lecture index was reachable; no transcript or notes text was retrievable, so nothing could be read and nothing is claimed from them

NPTEL Computer Architecture and Organization lectures 44-50 cover I/O organisation, data transfer techniques, interrupt handling twice and DMA, plus a set of I/O transfer exercises - the best-matched sequence found - but only the index page was readable
Anshul Kumar's IIT Delhi I/O subsystem lectures (33-37) are a strong candidate for the interface/bus angle, but again only titles were readable
a 12-minute Hindi lesson on the DMA controller and its modes; the page shows only the course index and the lesson is behind a login, so no content could be read
a Hindi DMA lecture found by search; no caption track was retrievable, so it could not be read and is not cited
an aggregation of COA question links with no teaching of its own; used only to locate questions
the memory-mapped I/O, cycle-stealing slowdown and DMA-mode questions on these pages are ISRO CSE papers, not GATE CSE; excluded from the PYQ set even though three of them are well formed
the 'highest I/O bandwidth' question on DMA modes is from the GATE IT 2006 paper, not GATE CSE, so it is not published as a CSE PYQ
indexes used to enumerate the topic's questions and their year/paper references; not used as answer sources wherever an accepted-answer page existed

third-party solution pages used only for 2021 Set 2, 2024 Set 1, 2024 Set 2, 2025 Set 1 and 2026 Set 2, where GATE Overflow had no accepted-answer page opened; their 'official key' claims are recorded as their claim, and every answer used from them was recomputed here

standard_refs: Stallings, Computer Organization and Architecture: Designing for Performance, ch. 7 (sections 7.1-7.5), the reference the NPTEL lectures themselves set for this module
Hamacher, Vranesic and Zaky, Computer Organization, ch. 4, for the interrupt cycle and the DMA bus-request/grant protocol
Patterson and Hennessy, Computer Organization and Design, ch. 6, for memory-mapped I/O and DMA/cache coherence
Official GATE CSE 2027 syllabus, Computer Organization and Architecture line: 'I/O interface (interrupt and DMA)'
